messages:
morgan: heads up — saw steady resident memory growth on the kv cache host after a long-context run (12k tokens). not sure if it's fragmentation or GC delay. attaching quick profiler dump.

morgan: profiler snippet:
```
KVAllocator: total_alloc=12.4G resident=11.8G free_frag=832M hole_count=1549
block_sizes: 4k=120k 16k=30k 64k=6k 256k=900 1M=48
compaction_threads=2 compaction_pending=0
last_compact_ts=2087649000
```

morgan: observed pattern: repeated tiny allocations for prefix tokens (4k) interleaved with occasional 1M allocations for long attention slices. over time the free_frag ballooned. :grimacing:

avani: ugh. thanks for the dump. do you have heapmap snapshot + live pages? curious about fragmentation map vs eviction activity.

morgan: i grabbed /proc/pagemap and a lightweight heaplet map. rough heatmap shows many scattered 4k holes between 1M blocks. looks like allocator buddy rounding causes misalignment when large/reuse happens.

ramon: can you paste the exact sequence of ops that created the pattern? was it: warm prefix -> spike long ctx -> drop -> repeat? or more interleaved?

morgan: sequence = repeated chat sessions: 1) short context (few tokens) -> 2) long generation (10-15k tokens pinned) -> 3) immediate drop to short again. cycles every ~30s for load test.

dina: Might be the worst-case for our current block size mix. 1M buckets are sparse — when long ctx allocs are freed, the leftover 4k pieces are left scattered. We should test tuning 256k and 1M thresholds.

ramon: proposed quick experiment: change small-block allocation policy to favor slab pooling for 4k/16k so they don't stab into large block free lists. Also try eager coalesce pass on free that gets triggered when fragmentation > X (say 20%).

morgan: agreed. also saw that compaction wasn't triggered because compaction_pending==0. compaction uses LRU of holes — maybe holes are too small to be worth collecting under current heuristic.

avani: can we add a transient compaction mode for long-context workloads that runs a fast sweep after a long-gen completes? e.g., if avg_alloc_size over last N secs > Y then trigger mini-compact.

ramon: yeah — add a "post-large-release" compaction. cheap approach: scan buddy-index for <chunk_count_threshold and do local defrag. cheaper than global compaction.

morgan: running a patch locally that: 1) adjusts block split threshold to stop allocating 4k from 1M unless > 75% used, 2) adds post-large-release compaction window = 5s. will run synthetic cycles.

kv-bot: deploy-bot: started test-run 2087654340 on test-kv-03 (morgan/ramon). logs will stream to /artifacts/kv-reclaim-exp/2087654340.tar.gz

dina: reasonable. also consider a reuse cache for recently-freed 4k fragments keyed by alignment/adjacent-run to improve locality rather than returning to buddy free lists.

ramon: good idea — small LRU freelist per-thread for common sizes (4k/16k) could cut cross-thread interference. we already have per-core arenas, but the scavenger policy is too conservative.

morgan: results from first run: memory plateaued at ~9.9G resident instead of 11.8G, free_frag down to 312M, hole_count=412. throughput unchanged.

avani: that's promising. can you attach perf flame for alloc/free hot paths? curious if compaction costs spike latency.

morgan: flame: compaction sweeps added ~0.8ms p50 during the 5s window, p99 unaffected. no visible stall in token generation.

dina: nice. next: run with mixed real traffic trace (chat + long-batch infer) for 1h to check long-tail regressions. also test with quantized kernels memory patterns — they sometimes change allocation stride.

ramon: operational note: if we enable post-large-release compaction in prod, we should gate by memory pressure and by tenant tier — cheaper to enable for Dedicated customers first.

avani: +1. Also add metric: frag_ratio = free_frag / resident and emit alert if > 0.25 for 10m.

morgan: will open PR with patch + test harness and results. thinking of two follow-ups: 1) micro-bench for freelist reuse patterns, 2) explore compact-on-alloc heuristic for very old holes.

ramon: sounds good. can you tag the PR with perf/regression checks so CI runs the 1h mixed trace? @dina can you help with the trace?

dina: on it. i'll prepare the trace and run the CI job.

morgan: thanks all. saving logs to /artifacts/kv-reclaim-exp/2087654321/ ; will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
